initial.reason: Monomer1 is a diglycidyl ether based on a bisphenol-like core (two epoxide rings: one explicitly as C1OC1 and a second as C4OC4). The aromatic, tertiary-carbon (bisphenol) backbone raises rigidity and Tg toward ~80°C while providing two epoxy reactive sites for crosslinking. Monomer2 is diethylenetriamine (NCCNCCN) — synthesizable, contains the required NC motif at least twice, and provides multiple amine nucleophiles for efficient epoxy ring-opening (high crosslink density to raise Er toward ~50 MPa). The epoxy (C1OC1/C4OC4) — amine (NC) pairing is chemically compatible for thermoset formation; this combination balances aromatic rigidity and multifunctional curing to approach the target Tg and Er.

best.reason: Revised to address feedback: monomer1 is a flexible diglycidyl ether (two epoxide rings shown as C1OC1 and C2OC2) to lower Tg via ether-rich aliphatic linkers while providing at least two epoxy reactive sites for crosslinking. Monomer2 is triethylenetetramine (NCCNCCNCCN) with multiple NC motifs (>=2) and four nitrogens to increase crosslink-supporting reactive site density and raise Er. The pair is epoxy–amine compatible (C1OC1 vs NC). These changes lower network stiffness/Tg (more flexible monomer1) while increasing crosslink density/Er (multifunctional polyamine), addressing the reported high-Tg and low-Er issues.
